Where it began

Marco Jansen was born in Klerksdorp on 1 May 2000, and he grew up with a ready-made practice partner: his twin brother Duan, who also went on to play for North West. As a boy Marco was an opening batter, and at nine he made 164 not out in a 20-over game, which tells you something about the bowling in that particular match.

He came through with North West, playing his first List A game for them in April 2018 and his first first-class match that October. In his first season of three-day cricket he was their leading wicket-taker, with 27 in six matches, and early in 2019 he was picked for South Africa's Under-19 tour of India.

The player

His Test debut came on Boxing Day 2021, at home against India, and Jasprit Bumrah, held at third slip, was the first name in his wicket column. By November 2026 he had played 23 Tests, taking 99 wickets at 20.81 and making 770 runs at 25.67, with five fifties and a best of 93. He also held 25 catches.

Two matches stand out. At Kingsmead in Durban in late 2024 he took 7 for 13 as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 42, the lowest total in their Test history, and he became the first South African to take ten wickets in a Test on that ground. A year later, in the second Test in India, he made 93 and took 6 for 48 and 1 for 23. South Africa won by 408 runs and took the series 2–0, their first series win in India for 25 years. He was also part of the squad that won the World Test Championship for 2023 to 2025.

What made him special

A left-arm quick who batted right-handed, he gave South Africa a genuine all-rounder. With the ball his wickets came at barely more than 20 runs apiece. With the bat he could change a game quickly: in a Twenty20 international against India in November 2024 he reached fifty in 16 balls, the second-quickest by a South African.

If there was a gap in his game, it was the missing Test hundred. Five fifties and a 93 suggest it was a matter of patience rather than talent.

Away from the middle

He became a familiar figure on the franchise circuit, playing in the Indian Premier League for Mumbai Indians, Sunrisers Hyderabad and Punjab Kings, in the SA20 for Sunrisers Eastern Cape, and in the first season of Major League Cricket in the United States for Washington Freedom. His first wicket in the IPL was Glenn Maxwell. He also played in the 2023 World Cup in India and the 2024 Twenty20 World Cup, where South Africa reached the final.

And finally

In November 2026, after 23 Tests, he had 99 wickets, one short of a round hundred. For a man who opened the batting as a boy and made 164 not out at nine, being left one short may have felt like an unusual position.
